players.product: electroplating chemistry for advanced packaging & substrates (MacDermid Alpha)

quarterly_data.signal: Record Q2 2026: organic net sales grew 15% (third consecutive quarter of double-digit organic growth), constant currency adjusted EBITDA up 33%, adjusted EPS up 27%; Electronics segment organic net sales +20% with every vertical up double digits; adjusted EBITDA margin excluding pass-through metals 27.8%, up 120 basis points, and would have been nearly 30% excluding above-target incentive compensation (over $10 million).
quarterly_data.figure: organic sales +15%; Electronics organic +20%; adj. EBITDA +33% cc; adj. EPS +27%; margin ex-metals 27.8%

quarterly_data.signal: Semiconductor Solutions organic net sales grew 31%: improved order patterns for power electronics products, growing momentum in thermal interface materials for high-power applications such as AI GPUs and CPUs, and strong and growing demand for advanced packaging solutions from OSATs in Asia. Power electronics and wafer plating both saw volume growth in the high teens; of the 30+% organic growth, 60% to two-thirds was volume and the rest price/mix from silver and gold input prices.
quarterly_data.figure: Semiconductor Solutions organic +31%; wafer plating and power electronics volume +high teens

quarterly_data.signal: Circuitry Solutions net sales +15% organically on metallization solutions tied to AI infrastructure and high-performance compute as customers add capacity for increasingly complex PCB architectures; Assembly Solutions +18% organically on higher-reliability solder paste in Asia and engineered preform materials used in data center applications; India growing robustly on supply-chain diversification.

Advanced packaging (quantified as several hundred million dollars of revenue) is performing quite well with share gain in the IC substrate / package substrate part of circuitry, strong high-end paste and wafer-level packaging; Element is establishing processes of record for the transition from CoWoS to CoPoS and other emerging technologies expected to ramp about 18 months from now, and expects the advanced packaging business to accelerate into 2027 and 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: advanced packaging several hundred million dollars of revenue; CoWoS-to-CoPoS ramp ~18 months out

quarterly_data.signal: Cuprion (active copper for thermal management, power delivery and plating copper on challenging substrates): the first Fremont plant is sampling and qualifying material with customers with plans to raise its throughput; the scope of the second Fremont site increased and progress was made toward a third site in Connecticut, so capacity expected by year-end 2027 rose materially during the quarter; customers are pulling the product aggressively, which should translate into material revenue and profit contribution in 2027 and a very robust 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure (capacity by YE2027 raised materially)

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance raised: full-year adjusted EBITDA $690 million-$710 million; Q3 adjusted EBITDA approximately $180 million with demand sequentially similar to the first half, no typical smartphone seasonal ramp assumed, raw material and logistics inflation from the conflict in Iran and modest Micromax softening; 2026 adjusted EPS growth approximately 20%.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 adj. EBITDA $690 million-$710 million; Q3 ~$180 million; adj. EPS growth ~20%

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity: capex $28 million in the quarter, over $50 million year-to-date, now roughly $100 million for the year (under 3% of sales), accelerating investment in Cuprion and thermal interface materials for hyperscale customers plus plant consolidation. Element is not capacity constrained in semi by and large, but is capacity constrained in TIMs and other engineered materials and is adding capacity as fast as it can; it is taking sticky share where it is first to market or where under-capitalized local competitors cannot float metal at current prices.

Across electronics customers capacity is being added: device assemblers and EMS shops, printed circuit board fabs in and outside China, huge investments in Taiwan and Korea, and semi fabs expanding at the leading edge; utilization is very high at the advanced end, supporting substantial capacity additions at leading-edge circuit board fabs, semi foundries and device assemblers. Management does not see this abating in the near term.

Acquisitions: Micromax contributed approximately $130 million to reported sales (roughly two-thirds metals) and is ahead of plan; EFC Gases & Advanced Materials contributed $16 million with conviction in $30 million for full-year 2026 on electronics, satellite and electrical-infrastructure demand. Pending merger with Solstice Advanced Materials carries over $180 million of cost synergy potential and remains subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals. Net leverage 2.9x pro forma, expected to reach roughly 2.5x by year-end.
quarterly_data.figure: Micromax ~$130 million sales; EFC $16 million (FY $30 million); Solstice synergies over $180 million; leverage 2.9x -> ~2.5x
